title: Graphic Design - Level II
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 16S/24Q to fewer than 30S/45Q units

program.section_heading: Graphic Design - Level II Certificate of Achievement
outcomes: Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to combine principles and elements of design with industry standard software and hardware to complete effective communication design work involving critical thinking for the graphic design industry.
Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to create and assess professional quality advertising, marketing, and other commercial work.
Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to design and brand for specific industries and audiences, including self-branding for their field of choice.

Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to select, prepare, and assemble a portfolio of work in digital and print formats, that represents individual interests and strengths for use in entering a four-year institution, professional art school, or professional field of choice.
careers: production, layout, content, publication, print, advertising or social media graphic designer

notes: The catalog prints 'Required Courses (Total 28)', but the nine courses listed directly under it sum to 25 units. The 28 appears to cover the whole program, including List A (25 + 3). It is recorded as the program total and as the Required Courses block's stated total; a reviewer should confirm.
No separate program total is printed other than the Required Courses total of 28.
Codes are written as the catalog prints them, without a space (e.g., ARTB4). Each one matches a closed-list code (e.g., ART B4), so none is marked as a catalog addition.

Careers come from the program description. The job titles are printed as one elliptical list ('production, layout, content, publication, print, advertising or social media graphic designer') and are kept as a single entry. 'communication arts' and 'graphic design' come from 'the communication arts and graphic design fields'.

Each outcome is copied with its embedded opening phrase 'Upon successful completion of the program, ...' because that phrase is part of each printed outcome rather than a separate lead-in; only the list numbers are removed.
The text ends with a 'PATHWAY EXPLORATION' heading that has no content.
